project.title: Gesture-Controlled Music Stem Mixer
project.one_liner: Live webcam hand-gesture control over a song's vocal/instrumental volume and EQ, using a self-trained gesture classifier on MediaPipe hand landmarks, mixing pre-separated Demucs stems in real time.
project.graded_contribution: The trained gesture-landmark classifier: self-collected dataset, custom preprocessing, own MLP architecture, training pipeline, and evaluation. MediaPipe (hand tracking) and Demucs (stem separation) are explicitly pretrained, off-the-shelf components -- not the contribution.
project.not_using: Spotify Web Playback SDK -- audio is DRM-protected, raw PCM never exposed. Local audio files only (mp3/wav via file picker).

mediapipe_hands.role: Detects up to 2 hands per frame, outputs 21 (x, y) landmark points per hand in pixel coordinates. Off-the-shelf, not trained or fine-tuned by us.
mediapipe_hands.version: mediapipe==0.10.21 (legacy Solutions API -- pinned below 1.0.0, which removed mp.solutions in favor of the newer Tasks API)

demucs.role: Source separation: splits a full song into vocals.wav and no_vocals.wav (instrumental) stems. Off-the-shelf pretrained model (htdemucs), not trained by us.
demucs.performance_note: CPU: ~2.2x song length to separate (measured: 3m5s song -> 6m51s). GPU (CUDA, RTX 3050): ~20x faster than CPU (same song -> 20.6s). Separation results are cached on disk per song so repeat plays are instant.

the_trained_classifier.what_it_is: A custom MLP that classifies a single hand's pose from its 21 MediaPipe landmarks into one of 7 gesture classes.

dataset.collection_method: Self-recorded via a modified version of the base repo's app.py: press a class number to arm continuous per-frame logging of that class (originally hold-to-record, later changed to a tap-to-toggle latch so recording doesn't depend on OS key-repeat timing), varying hand, angle, distance, and lighting across takes.

class_meanings.neutral: relaxed/resting hand -- also absorbs undefined shapes like a closed fist or thumbs-up so they don't get misread as a real command
class_meanings.one: index finger only extended -- mode-select: Music Player Controls
class_meanings.two: index+middle extended (peace sign) -- mode-select: Vocals & Instrumental
class_meanings.stop_play: flat palm facing camera, fingers extended AND held together (classic 'stop sign') -- universal play/pause, works in any mode

dataset.notable_iteration: stop_play was first defined as an open hand with fingers SPREAD apart, which overlapped heavily with pinch_open in landmark space (recall only 0.43, precision 0.62) and dragged down overall accuracy to 89.1%. Redefining it as fingers held TOGETHER (classic stop-sign) fixed the overlap: recall rose to 0.98, precision to 0.86, and overall accuracy recovered to 95.4%. Good example of a data/label-design fix outperforming more data of the same (broken) definition.

steps: 1. Subtract the wrist landmark (index 0) from all 21 landmarks -> translation invariant (hand position in frame doesn't matter)
2. Divide all 42 resulting values by their own max absolute value -> scale invariant (distance from camera doesn't matter)
3. Flatten to a 42-length feature vector (21 landmarks x 2 coords)
preprocessing.why: Raw pixel coordinates encode irrelevant variance (where in frame, how close to camera); normalizing removes that so the model can focus on hand shape, the actual signal.

architecture.layers: Input(42) -> Dropout(0.2) -> Dense(128, relu) -> Dropout(0.4) -> Dense(64, relu) -> Dense(7, softmax)
architecture.regularization: Dropout at two points specifically to fight overfitting on a dataset this size

training_config.split: 70% train / 15% validation / 15% test, stratified by class

failure_analysis: pinch_closed -> one: 26 samples confused. Both involve a partially curled hand with the index finger relatively prominent; overlap is the main remaining weak point (recall 0.76 for pinch_closed).
neutral -> stop_play: 20 samples confused. Both are 'open hand facing camera' at a coarse level; fine-grained finger-together-vs-relaxed distinction is the residual ambiguity.
one's precision (0.85) is the lowest precision score -- it absorbs some misclassifications from neighboring classes (pinch_closed, stop_play) rather than being confused with something else itself.

the_trained_classifier.export: Converted to TensorFlow Lite with default post-training quantization (tf.lite.TFLiteConverter, Optimize.DEFAULT) for fast per-frame inference in the live app.

abandoned_approach_ablation.what_was_tried: A second classifier (point_history_classifier) on a 16-frame trajectory of the thumb tip, to detect clockwise/counterclockwise rotation for a 'volume knob' gesture.
why_it_failed: Initial slow, deliberate circular motion: CW/CCW were statistically indistinguishable (raw single-frame signed-area separation, mean/std ratio ~0.11 for clockwise) -- 62-66% accuracy on a 4-class problem, both plain MLP and LSTM architectures plateaued at the same level, confirming it was a data/signal problem, not a model-capacity problem.

Faster, more deliberate motion improved raw signal ~20-40x (validated via a geometric signed-area sanity check before retraining) and got a 2-class CW/CCW diagnostic model to 77.8% balanced accuracy -- workable but not reliable enough for continuous control.

Even after that improvement, live testing showed inconsistent left/right hand behavior and rotation direction being fundamentally hard to execute/detect reliably, especially since MediaPipe's hand tracking itself degrades during the fast motion the gesture requires (motion blur), i.e. fighting the tracker's own limitations.
abandoned_approach_ablation.resolution: Rotation-based control was dropped entirely for live use. Replaced with two purely geometric (untrained, deterministic) mappings instead: pinch-distance ratio (thumb-to-index / hand-scale) for continuous 0-1 volume, and a single-frame wrist-to-thumb-tip tilt angle for continuous -5..+5 EQ boost/cut. Both are static per-frame measurements rather than motion trajectories, which sidesteps the tracking-during-motion problem entirely and requires no training data.
abandoned_approach_ablation.why_this_belongs_in_the_report: Demonstrates a full methodology cycle: hypothesis -> data collection -> two architectures tried -> root-cause diagnosis (via a geometric ground-truth sanity check, not just retrying) -> informed decision to replace ML with a simpler, more reliable deterministic method where the geometry genuinely didn't need learning. Good ablation/discussion material, not a hidden failure.

modes.mode_select_mechanism: Hold a mode-select pose (one/two/three) for ~1s; a majority-vote window (needs 60%+ agreement over ~20 frames) confirms the switch, tolerating an occasional misclassified frame instead of resetting on any single flicker.

vocals_and_instrumental.control: Continuous thumb-index pinch distance per hand (left=vocals, right=instrumental), directly mapped 0-1, no classifier involved in the control itself -- pure geometry.
vocals_and_instrumental.gated_to: Only updates when that hand's pose is pinch_open, pinch_closed, or neutral -- ignores mode-select/stop_play poses so switching gestures doesn't bleed into the gain.

bass_and_treble.control: Wrist-to-thumb-tip tilt angle per hand (left=bass, right=treble), a single-frame static angle (not a motion trajectory), mapped to -5 (cut) .. +5 (boost) around a thumb-up = 0 neutral reference. Drives real low-shelf (150Hz) / high-shelf (4000Hz) biquad EQ filters (RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook formulas) applied to the mixed output, up to +-12dB.
bass_and_treble.gated_to: Only updates when that hand's pose is classified as neutral (the thumbs-up/relaxed shape) -- exclusive to that pose so other hand shapes don't move the EQ.

music_player.control: Not finalized -- an initial fast-swipe ('shooing') gesture attempt failed because MediaPipe's tracking degrades during the fast motion the gesture itself requires (motion blur), same root issue as the abandoned rotation classifier.

universal_gestures.note: Work in any mode, detected independent of the mode-select state machine.
universal_gestures.stop_play: Trained classifier pose (see above), majority-vote tolerant hold (~2.3-2.5s) plus a wall-clock cooldown (2s) after firing so relaxing out of the pose doesn't immediately re-trigger.
universal_gestures.add_song: 'Absolute Cinema' pose: geometric, not trained -- requires (a) wrist-to-wrist distance > 6x average hand scale AND (b) both hands classified as open/spread (fingers extended and apart), so raising both hands to do bass/treble tilting doesn't accidentally trigger it. Opens a native file picker (tkinter), defaulting to a Songs/ folder; any newly picked song is copied into that folder and separated once, then cached for instant reload.

audio_engine.mixing: sounddevice OutputStream callback mixes vocals.wav + no_vocals.wav with independently smoothed gains (exponential smoothing per audio block to avoid clicks from gesture jitter).
audio_engine.eq: Real low-shelf/high-shelf biquad filters (scipy.signal.lfilter, RBJ cookbook coefficients), recomputed each audio block from the smoothed dB target, filter state (zi) carried across blocks per channel for click-free continuity.
audio_engine.transport: play/pause via stopping/starting the actual audio stream in place (position preserved); seek() adjusts playback position directly, clamped to track bounds.
audio_engine.threading: Camera/gesture loop and audio callback run on separate threads; only two floats (target gains) and two floats (target EQ) cross between them, guarded by a lock. No heavy computation inside the audio callback itself.

functionality.ui: OpenCV overlay: translucent HUD bars, live gain bars (0-1) for vocals/instrumental, centered bars (-5..+5) for bass/treble, song name + play state + elapsed/total time, mode indicator, persistent on-screen gesture legend, and a toggleable (`d` key) debug readout of raw geometric values for live calibration.

mediapipe.purpose: Pretrained hand landmark detection (21 points x 2 hands)

tensorflow.purpose: Training and running the custom MLP classifier; TFLite export/inference

opencv-python.purpose: Webcam capture, drawing the UI/HUD overlay, keyboard input for the data-logging tool

numpy.purpose: Landmark preprocessing, geometric calculations (pinch ratio, tilt angle, wrist distance)

matplotlib.purpose: Confusion matrix plotting in the training notebook

scipy.purpose: Bass/treble shelf-filter biquad coefficients and real-time filtering (signal.lfilter)

sounddevice.purpose: Real-time low-latency audio output stream for the live mixer

soundfile.purpose: Reading the separated vocals.wav / no_vocals.wav stem files

torch.purpose: Backend for Demucs; CUDA build used for GPU-accelerated separation (~20x faster than CPU)

tkinter.purpose: Native file picker for song selection, no extra dependency

deep_learning_techniques_used: Supervised multi-class classification (custom MLP, not a pretrained/fine-tuned network)
Feature engineering / preprocessing for translation and scale invariance on landmark coordinates
Dropout regularization to control overfitting on a moderately sized self-collected dataset
Post-training quantization (TFLite) for efficient real-time CPU inference

Ablation methodology: a second architecture (LSTM) tried for a different sub-problem (rotation direction), compared against a plain MLP, both evaluated against a geometric ground-truth baseline to diagnose whether the limitation was model capacity or data/signal quality

Confusion-matrix-driven iterative dataset design (identifying a class-overlap problem, redefining the class's pose definition, and re-validating rather than just adding more data of the same definition)
abstract_and_report_checklist: Self-collected dataset description: 7 classes, ~14.6k samples, collection methodology (webcam, varied angle/distance/lighting, tap-to-arm continuous logging), contributor notes
Preprocessing justification (wrist-relative translation + max-abs scale normalization, and why: removes irrelevant variance)
Architecture description (42 -> 128 -> 64 -> 7 MLP, dropout placement, param count)
Final accuracy, full confusion matrix, per-class precision/recall/F1
Failure analysis: pinch_closed/one overlap, neutral/stop_play overlap, and the earlier stop_play pose-redefinition story as a worked example of diagnosing and fixing a class-overlap problem
Ablation: the abandoned rotation classifier -- MLP vs LSTM vs geometric ground-truth comparison, and why a deterministic geometric method replaced it in the final system
Explicit statement that MediaPipe and Demucs are pretrained components; the trained MLP classifier is the original contribution
System-level description: mode state machine, universal gestures, real-time audio engine (mixing + EQ), threading model
Performance note: GPU vs CPU separation benchmark (20x speedup) as a practical engineering result worth mentioning
Limitations: Demucs stem bleed (imperfect separation, inherent to the pretrained model, not the classifier), Player-mode controls not finalized, bass/treble neutral-point calibration is per-user
